title: Composable timeout-slice streaming connector and Go SDK cancellation ergonomics
creator: Maya Patel
description: Add a composable timeout-slice layer to the Go SDK streaming connector to make context cancellation and per-message deadlines explicit, deterministic, and ergonomic for client code. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, benchmarks, and example patterns for graceful drain and forceful cancel semantics.
background: Current streaming helpers in the Go SDK conflate transport-level timeouts, message-level deadlines, and client-level cancellation which leads to races during connection pool handoff and graceful shutdown. Field reports and customer issues show intermittent hung streams when upstream cancels during mid-response and when autoscaler moves connections. We need a clearer API that composes: overall request timeout, per-message deadline, and cooperative drain window so callers can choose graceful vs immediate termination. Goal is to provide safe defaults and examples for common patterns.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike — prototyped 'TimeoutSlice' abstraction which composes context.WithDeadline windows for: (a) connect, (b) initial response, (c) per-message read. Prototype lives in internal/streaming/timeoutslice

2026-02-21: Implementation — added StreamSession and MessageCtx helpers in pkg/stream; introduced WithStreamTimeout(ctx, slices...) helper to build layered deadlines without losing parent cancellation

2026-02-25: Tests — wrote unit tests for cancellation propagation and EarlyCancel scenario. Discovered race when connection is returned to pool while goroutine still reading; added a lease token on StreamConn to prevent reuse until drain completes

2026-03-02: Performance — microbenchmarks show 5-8% overhead on happy-path per-message latency due to additional context allocation. Added pooling for message contexts to reduce allocations; end-to-end throughput impact within 2% under typical load

2026-03-05: Integration — e2e tests against staging runtime. Found behavior where WithStreamTimeout per-message short deadlines caused partial responses and left KV cache entries inconsistent; added explicit KV cache eviction on mid-stream cancel
2026-03-08: PR created and CI is green for unit/integration tests, running full load bench overnight: PR #1427
decisions: Expose two top-level helpers: WithStreamTimeout(ctx, slices...) for callers who want to supply explicit slices, and StreamContextDefaults() which returns safe defaults used by SDK methods.
Default behavior: 30s overall request timeout, 10s initial response, per-message deadline = min(remaining, 5s) with 100ms jitter for retry alignment.
Make drain cooperative: consumer signals Done() and waits up to DrainWindow (default 250ms) before force-cancel. Expose WithDrainWindow(ctx, duration) for advanced users.
Maintain backward compatibility: high-level Generate/Chat helpers use StreamContextDefaults; low-level streaming client exposes new APIs for advanced control.
Optional lease token on StreamConn prevents pool reuse until the previous stream's readers exit; this avoids connection handoff races seen in integration tests.
review_comments: PM review (Anika Sharma): prefer safe defaults for enterprise customers; document trade-offs for optimistic drain vs strong SLA requirements
Design review (Liam O'Connor): suggested removing jitter for per-message deadlines in deterministic test mode; added TestDeterministic flag
Security review (Priya Nambiar): verify that context metadata (auth headers) is not leaked during lease handoff; added unit test to assert headers are reset
Infra note (Owen Kim): connection lease may increase transient GPU attach latency; monitor allocation percentiles post-rollout

Unit tests cover cancellation propagation, drain window behavior, lease token handoff, and header reset on reuse
Integration tests against staging runtime show no increase in 99th percentile tail latency beyond 5% and no new connection leak failures
Benchmark dashboard updated and perf regressions addressed (<=2% throughput loss on typical workloads)
